issues.body: `lane_admission()` correctly treats ELIGIBLE as only an upper bound because registry provenance is unreadable, but `decide()` still returns `flag` for that population. Renaming the state and disclaiming enrollment in an internal reason string cannot change the externally persisted meaning of `review:unreviewed`, which AGENTS.md and this module define as "enrolled, awaiting review". Thus a worker-shaped same-repo bot PR with no provenance record is still presented to every label consumer as enrolled. `registry-lane-unconfirmed` only counts the ambiguity after it ages and does not remove or correct the misleading label. This is materially the same correctness gap as round 3.
issues.fix_hint: Do not add `review:unreviewed` from ELIGIBLE alone. Require an authoritative registry-produced enrollment/provenance signal before applying an enrollment-shaped label, or introduce a distinct label whose public semantics are explicitly "author-side eligible, enrollment unconfirmed" and update every census and consumer accordingly. Add a real-path test proving that an eligible PR lacking registry provenance never receives an enrollment-shaped label; a separate age-based alarm may still report it.
issues.title: ELIGIBLE PRs are still labelled as enrolled without provenance

verdict.summary: Round 4 adds more explicit documentation, tests, and a time-based census for the provenance-unknown residual, but the load-bearing correctness issue is unchanged. `decide()` still writes `review:unreviewed` for every merely ELIGIBLE PR even though ELIGIBLE expressly does not establish registry enrollment and the repository defines that label as meaning "enrolled, awaiting review". A later census can reveal an aging uncertain population, but it neither prevents nor repairs the false persisted state. The same major finding remains, so progress is stagnant.
